findings.desc: CHK-002 correctly single-sourced production code (bare '.lattice' now only at brand-paths.ts:72/:78, verified), but 52 files under packages/main/src/tasks still hardcode '.lattice' when BUILDING test fixtures — roughly 180 occurrences, e.g. deprecated-gc-smoke.ts:39 mkdirSync(join(tmp,'.lattice')) then resolveAuditConfig(tmp). These are not cosmetic: the fixture WRITES the deprecated dir while production code READS via the resolver, so the moment CHK-003 flips PROOF_OR_STOP_STATE_DIR to '.proof-or-stop' the fixture and the reader disagree and these smokes fail. I verified the hazard fix works by simulating the rename (flipping the constant made isStoryMetadataPath return true for BOTH dirs, so archives stay excluded from storyFilesHash) — that part is sound. This finding is about the fixture-side gap the simulation did not exercise, since I reverted before running the suite. CHK-003 must either route fixture construction through STATE_DIR_NAMES/the resolver, or explicitly accept that these smokes get updated in the same commit as the move. Raising as high because discovering it mid-move on 7580 files is exactly the interruption CHK-008's abort path exists for.

thin-init-assets-smoke.ts:200 and :206 assert /lattice codex verify/ while the assertion MESSAGE and the actual template both say 'proof-or-stop codex verify'. The regex and the message disagree, so the test passes for the wrong reason or fails once the template is correct — the same message-vs-assertion mismatch class as B-cdf6:F-047, where a doesNotMatch message said 'must reference proof-or-stop' while the regex checked 'lattice'. Found by the CHK-004 implementer, which correctly did NOT widen scope: this is the bin-NAME token, and bin names are CHK-006's domain. Assigning to CHK-006, which already owns bin/lattice.js removal and must reconcile every bin-name assertion in the same commit.

CHK-003 first attempt FAILED and was aborted; recording the exact failure mode so the retry is designed, not improvised. What I did: git mv .lattice -> .proof-or-stop plus .lattice-codex -> .proof-or-stop-codex (7611 files, all status R), updated .gitignore, pointed proof-or-stop.config.json storyDir at the new path, and flipped PROOF_OR_STOP_STATE_DIR/ADAPTER_DIR to canonical. Paths then resolved correctly (verified: STATE_DIR=.proof-or-stop, STORY_DIR=.proof-or-stop/story/actives, config.storyDir matching) but story_get returned {story: null} for BOTH era archives. ROOT CAUSE: the CLI writes .proof-or-stop/activity.jsonl on every invocation, and because I ran diagnostic commands while the rename was staged-but-uncommitted, BOTH directories existed simultaneously — CHK-008's documented half-done abort condition. I then made it worse: rm -rf .lattice deleted working-tree files whose renamed counterparts existed only in the index, not yet on disk, so the archives vanished from the working tree while remaining correct in the index (7583 staged paths under story/actives). git checkout-index -a -f did NOT restore them. RECOVERY: content was intact in the HEAD commit (verified via git cat-file -e and git show), and CHK-008's abort (git reset HEAD + git checkout -- .) restored all 344 archives with the tree clean and B-0168 readable at its pre-move phase INIT. Zero data loss. LESSONS FOR THE RETRY: (1) commit the rename atomically BEFORE running any CLI command, since every invocation writes activity.jsonl and recreates the old dir; (2) never rm -rf the old dir while renames are merely staged; (3) the half-done detector fires on runtime write-back, not only on interrupted moves, so it needs a 'is the old dir merely a gitignored runtime leftover' discriminator; (4) do the config/constant flip in the SAME commit as the mv, because a resolver pointing at the new path while files are staged-only is unreadable.

Two hardcoded .lattice paths survive CHK-003's move and both are verified live, not speculative. (1) cli-init.ts still writes Lattice.md under a hardcoded .lattice/ while the same init writes the manifest to .proof-or-stop/ — init therefore STRADDLES two state dirs, creating a stray legacy directory on every fresh init. Found by the CHK-006 implementer; I confirmed the literal is still present. This blocks thin-init-assets-smoke and verify-entrypoints.mjs. (2) runtime-artifact-registry.ts lists ONLY '.lattice/locks/' as a material-excluded runtime path, so the runtime now writes .proof-or-stop/locks/ into a directory git does not ignore — measured consequence: validate-execution-lock-smoke fails with unexpected_dirty_files=2. Both are the same defect class as F-001: a path probe pinned to one spelling. Assigned to CHK-007, which owns re-pinning and the residue-gate scan roots.

packages/main/src/core/acceptance-rollout.ts:362 hardcodes storyPath = `.lattice/story/actives/${storyId}/process-events.jsonl` (deprecated-only spelling, no read-both fallback, no brand-paths import) and passes it to `git show <metadataCommitSha>:<storyPath>` at line 363. This is the exact CHK-002 regression class the story documents (a comparison/read path hardcoding only the deprecated spelling): once a repo has fully migrated to .proof-or-stop/ and a NEW quorum commit is made post-migration, this git-show will always fail to find the path at that commit (process-events.jsonl now lives under .proof-or-stop/story/actives/...), throwing acceptance rollout observation errors for any post-migration commit. Should derive the path via brand-paths.ts (e.g. stateDirCandidates or PROOF_OR_STOP_STATE_DIR) and probe both candidate spellings against that specific historical commit (a plain existsSync canonical-first probe on the working tree is insufficient here because the path must be resolved AS OF that git commit, not the current working tree state).

concept-cleanup: state-dir read-both rename (CHK-002/CHK-003) is incomplete at the StoryStore discovery/read layer. packages/main/src/core/store.ts:64-68 builds legacyBaseDirs from only LEGACY_DOCS_STORY_DIR (docs/story/actives, a different older migration), never from PROOF_OR_STOP_STORY_DIR_NAMES (packages/main/src/core/lattice-paths.ts:41-43), which is the canonical read-both list this same story built specifically to enumerate every accepted spelling of the story dir, including .lattice/story/actives. That list is wired into evidence-freshness.ts (storyFilesHash exclusion) but NOT into store.ts (candidateStoryDirs at store.ts:111-113, listStoryIds at store.ts:241-247). Repro: a story archive still on disk under .lattice/story/actives/B-49ed/ (brought in by a main merge, INIT_CHECK-complete, files present) is fully invisible: story_get --storyId=B-49ed --slim --fields=story prints story:null at EXIT 0 (story-query.ts:481-483 swallows StoryArtifactMissingError into null), it never appears in session_brief's ledger, and it is entirely absent from listStoryIds(). This directly contradicts the story's own stated acceptance criterion in docs/requirements/decisions/proof-or-stop-identity-migration.md line 105 (All 344 archived story directories remain readable after migration) and the CHK-003 userSees claim (story_get succeeds against .proof-or-stop for archived stories). Compounding factor: story_get silently returns null/exit-0 instead of failing loud the way checklist_get does for the same story (checklist_get correctly errors non-zero naming both tried paths), so the read gap is invisible to a caller checking only the exit code.

CHK-008:adversarial:0 verificationEvidence (moveIsPureRenameCommit=true) does not actually establish the claimed intent ("git revert <sha> alone restores the pre-move layout with no manual fixup"). The real state-dir move required TWO commits: ec7f315e0a (matched by verify-migration-contract.mjs grep --grep=CHK-003: move state dirs, diffstat 0 insertions/0 deletions) landed the mv NESTED at .proof-or-stop/.lattice/... and also reverted the canonical PROOF_OR_STOP_STATE_DIR constant back to .lattice; the actual fix to the final canonical layout + constants is a SEPARATE commit 8c0bd7b87c (fix nested move + flip canonical dir constants, 523 insertions/73 deletions) that is NOT a pure rename. I safely reproduced: `git revert --no-commit ec7f315e0a` on current HEAD (4402ba9a7a) produces dozens of git file-location CONFLICT errors and a non-zero exit rather than a clean restore (aborted immediately, repo confirmed clean via git status --porcelain). The witness checks the diffstat of the wrong (superseded/defective) commit instead of testing actual end-to-end revertibility of the current HEAD, so a green moveIsPureRenameCommit=true does not discriminate a genuinely non-atomic, non-single-commit-revertible migration from an atomic one -- which is exactly the CHK-008 property it exists to prove.

CHK-003:adversarial:0 witness scripts/verify-state-dir-migration.mjs:49 uses a loose threshold (n > 7000) for trackedArchiveFiles instead of an exact expected count, so it would not catch a partial loss of up to several hundred archive files during the move (current count is 7583/7588). This check has only coarse discriminating power on its own; it is not the sole line of defense (the two named-archive readability + phase checks and the git log --follow check in the same script do have real discriminating power for content/history loss), so this is advisory rather than blocking.

CHK-005:adversarial:0 intent literally asks for a repo-wide grep for @lattice/core outside node_modules/dist/state-dir returning nothing, but scripts/verify-core-package-rename.mjs only checks packages/utils and packages/lab dependency declarations plus the root package.json name -- it does not grep the wider source tree (tests/fixtures/comments) for stray @lattice/core occurrences. I independently grepped and found the remaining occurrences are all legitimate deprecated-name compatibility literals (DEPRECATED_CORE_PACKAGE_NAME constants, fixture data, comments documenting the rename) rather than unmigrated real dependency declarations, so this is not a functional gap today, but the witness is narrower than the intent text describes and would not catch a genuinely stray @lattice/core dependency reference introduced outside utils/lab package.json in the future. Advisory, not blocking.

concept-cleanup: stale comment in packages/main/src/cli.ts:6 still tells the reader to use the generated bin/lattice.js bootstrap script for @lattice/utils helper tools. bin/lattice.js was deleted by this story (CHK-006); the generated bootstrap entrypoint is now bin/proof-or-stop.js (see bin/bootstrap-runner.js header, bin/proof-or-stop.js). This is misleading, live prose in a source comment that a developer reading cli.ts would follow to a Cannot-find-module dead end.

doc-code-drift: CLAUDE.md managed block (committed at ad5dc15253) hardcodes the literal `.lattice-codex/` path ("Codex assets live separately under `.lattice-codex/`") even though its own generation template packages/main/src/init-assets.ts:76 (CLAUDE_MD_TEMPLATE) correctly interpolates `${PROOF_OR_STOP_ADAPTER_DIR}` = `.proof-or-stop-codex` (brand-paths.ts:85). The materialized file was not regenerated from the current template after this story renamed the adapter dir. Mechanically confirmed: `node bin/proof-or-stop.js check` reports `STALE_SAFE CLAUDE.md: Proof-or-Stop managed section differs from template` right now on this worktree. Fix: run `proof-or-stop check --apply` (or hand-sync) so the committed CLAUDE.md matches the current template output.

doc-promise-undelivered / scope violation: commit ad5dc15253 (message: "test(CHK-005): register the OQ-2 boundary guard so it actually runs", body states "Scope: scripts block only") in fact deletes 1106 of 1118 lines from CLAUDE.md and 592 of 604 lines from AGENTS.md, permanently removing all project-specific process documentation this repo depends on (行为准则/Story lifecycle table/CLI cheatsheet/Reviewer opt-in routing/verification-intent rules/Handler coding convention/角色分工/etc.), replacing both files with only the 8-12 line managed block. No later commit in main...HEAD restores this content, and no equivalent content exists anywhere else in the working tree (grep for distinctive strings like "两条通道，状态机自动判定" and "禁止直接读写 docs/story" returns zero hits repo-wide). The story contract doc docs/requirements/decisions/proof-or-stop-identity-migration.md and plan.md CHK-006 authorize modifying CLAUDE.md only to remove stale bin/lattice.js references, not to delete unrelated project documentation. This is a severe undisclosed content-loss regression bundled into a commit whose own message claims a much narrower scope.

doc-code-drift: docs/requirements/decisions/proof-or-stop-identity-migration.md:183 (Known residual drift for CHK-007) claims "CLAUDE.md:192 still documents the old @lattice/core/dev-host import in its debug.ts example". doc-code-drift: CHANGELOG.md v0.3.261 entry (added by CHK-006 commit a5a75f7768/b27383a0fc) states "Not affected: the lattice npm bin alias ... and the @lattice/core package name are separate identities and remain retained." This is factually wrong at the time it was written: CHK-005 (commits 0eb0d46aff/ad5dc15253) landed BEFORE CHK-006 in this same story and already renamed packages/main/package.json name from @lattice/core to @proof-or-stop/core (verified: grep "name" packages/main/package.json now shows @proof-or-stop/core). No CHANGELOG entry anywhere documents the @lattice/core -> @proof-or-stop/core rename at all; the only mention of it is this one entry, and it asserts the opposite of what happened. A reader trusting the changelog would wrongly conclude the npm package identity is unchanged.

packages/main/src/core/prompt-registry.ts:309 renderCodexPromptContent() rewrites `.claude/agents/` to the DEPRECATED `.lattice-codex/agents/` (hardcoded literal, not derived from brand-paths.ts PROOF_OR_STOP_ADAPTER_DIR). This function is exercised by init-assets.ts renderCodexAgentContent() when materializing Codex-host prompt copies. Today it is a no-op because no template currently contains the literal `.claude/agents/`, but the transform explicitly exists to translate host-specific paths for Codex output, and if a future template (or the README template that shares this pipeline) references `.claude/agents/`, the Codex-rendered copy would silently emit the pre-migration `.lattice-codex/agents/` spelling instead of the canonical `.proof-or-stop-codex/agents/` — the exact regression class this story exists to close. Should read `${PROOF_OR_STOP_ADAPTER_DIR}/agents/` from brand-paths.ts.

doc-code-drift: packages/main/src/init-assets.ts LATTICE_CODEX_ADAPTER_MANIFEST (lines 170 and 201) still asserts "The deprecated bin/lattice-codex.js alias is retained and still works" and "...the bin/lattice-codex.js alias is deprecated but retained", with an in-code comment at line 198-200 explicitly saying this mention "is intentional and stays." This is now false: CHK-006 of this same story deleted bin/lattice-codex.js entirely (confirmed: file absent on disk, git diff main...HEAD -- bin/lattice-codex.js shows a pure deletion). This manifest is not just source code prose -- it materializes verbatim into .proof-or-stop-codex/lattice.json (the CHK-003/CHK-004 deliverable at the new adapter path in this very worktree), so the false claim ships as user/agent-facing content read by Proof-or-Stop tooling. init-assets.ts was last touched by CHK-007 (commit 2a2ad35268), which runs after CHK-006 in the dependency chain, so the stale text survived past the point where it became false. `node bin/proof-or-stop.js check` does not currently flag this drift.

concept-cleanup: docs/CLI.md describes the deprecated adapter-dir/manifest paths (.lattice-codex/lattice.json, .lattice/lattice.json) as CURRENT behavior with zero deprecation framing, contradicting CHK-003/CHK-004's canonical rename to .proof-or-stop-codex/proof-or-stop.json. Lines docs/CLI.md:1018-1023 (npm run test:codex-assets section) and docs/CLI.md:1131-1135 (Claude Code section) present .lattice-codex/lattice.json, .lattice-codex/settings.json, .lattice-codex/agents, and .lattice/lattice.json as the paths a reader should currently expect/consult -- not as retained-for-reads aliases. This story DID edit docs/CLI.md (CHK-006 bin-alias removal note) but left this separate, still-live section using the old spellings untouched, so a reader following docs/CLI.md verbatim after this migration lands would look for adapter state at the wrong (deprecated) path. Note: docs/CLI.md:1135 also contains what appears to be a leaked local absolute filesystem path (/Users/jek/Documents/Work/Orchestrate/...) in markdown link targets, unrelated to this migration but adjacent and worth cleaning in the same pass. Not caught by the automated brand-prose/brand-exec gates in scripts/verify-lattice-residue.mjs because those specifically scan for bare `lattice <cmd>` invocation prose, not stale path documentation.

packages/main/src/core/prompt-role-contract-registry.ts:132 and :167 hardcode relDir = host === 'claude' ? '.claude/agents' : '.lattice-codex/agents' -- the DEPRECATED-only adapter dir spelling, in the SAME FILE that correctly uses read-both adapterManifestCandidates() / stateDirCandidates() a few lines above (110-114, 88-90). This is the exact bug class the story targets: line 133 existsSync(join(projectRoot, relDir, file)) is the fallback branch of reviewerHostRenderSource() reached whenever the codex/global manifest does not resolve to package-registry/full-asset (e.g. a fully-migrated full-asset-mode Codex project with only canonical .proof-or-stop-codex/agents/*.md on disk and no promptMode/assetMode field). For such a project this existsSync would find nothing under the deprecated .lattice-codex/agents, misclassify source as package-registry, and line 170 'if (source === full-asset)' would then SKIP assertExactHostAsset entirely -- silently disabling the content-drift check that reviewerHostRenderIdentity() exists to provide (consumed by review_run_start and story_dispatch). Line 167 has the identical hardcoded literal feeding assertExactHostAsset's own join(). Should derive from PROOF_OR_STOP_ADAPTER_DIR / ADAPTER_DIR_NAMES in brand-paths.ts, probing both spellings like the manifest lookup above it already does.

concept-cleanup: packages/main/src/core/codex-adapter-checks.ts:401-404 and :420 hardcode the deprecated adapter-manifest path spelling in live, user-facing verify_codex/doctor check messages instead of deriving from the read-both resolver already used elsewhere in the same function. Line 404 (the global-thin branch, which is the one that actually fires in this repo -- confirmed live via `node bin/proof-or-stop.js verify_codex`) emits 'global-thin project: Codex adapter behavior runs from global lattice CLI (.lattice/lattice.json present)'; line 420's fail path emits 'missing .lattice-codex/lattice.json'. Both should read .proof-or-stop/proof-or-stop.json and .proof-or-stop-codex/proof-or-stop.json (the canonical names per CANONICAL_CODEX_MANIFEST_REL at line 373 = PROOF_OR_STOP_ADAPTER_DIR/PROOF_OR_STOP_MANIFEST_FILENAME, already correctly used by resolveCodexManifest() a few lines above in the same file). The comment directly above at line 401-402 ('Resolver priority: canonical .lattice/lattice.json first') is also stale for the same reason. This is exactly the regression class core/brand-paths.ts's own module header warns about: a hardcoded deprecated literal sitting inside an output/comparison string rather than flowing from the single resolver, so the canonical spelling never appears in output even after the rename ships.

packages/main/src/cli-init.ts:217 detectInitProfile()'s hasCodexMarkers = existsSync(join(root, 'AGENTS.md')) || existsSync(join(root, '.lattice-codex')) hardcodes the DEPRECATED-only adapter dir spelling (no brand-paths import, no ADAPTER_DIR_NAMES/adapterDirCandidates usage), even though this same file was heavily edited elsewhere in this diff for CHK-002/004/007 to use the resolver. On a project that has been fully migrated (canonical .proof-or-stop-codex/ present, no .lattice-codex/, and no AGENTS.md e.g. a thin/global-thin project without the AGENTS marker file), re-running init/init --upgrade would fail to auto-detect the existing Codex profile via the directory marker and could silently fall through to profile 'core' or 'claude', changing which assets init manages. Should use ADAPTER_DIR_NAMES.some(dir => existsSync(join(root, dir))) from brand-paths.ts, matching the read-both pattern used a few lines away by detectManagedAssetProfile() in managed-assets.ts.

packages/utils/src/handlers/tool-status.ts:57 runtimeLogPath = join(root, PROOF_OR_STOP_DIR, 'activity.jsonl') only checks the CANONICAL state dir; it has no fallback to the DEPRECATED spelling (.lattice/activity.jsonl) the way most other consumers in this diff do via STATE_DIR_NAMES. tool_status's own comment (line 4, 56) describes 'dual-source' as runtime-path + legacy docs/story/ path, and concatenates both when present (line 59), so a partially-migrated repo whose activity.jsonl still lives only under the deprecated .lattice/ (not yet re-written under .proof-or-stop/, e.g. right after this story's git-mv but before any command has run to recreate the file at the canonical path) would have that history silently excluded from tool_status output -- undercounting usage stats rather than erroring. Lower severity than the other findings since this is read-only reporting, not a correctness gate, but it is the same missed-consumer pattern: should iterate STATE_DIR_NAMES from brand-paths.ts (or lattice-paths.ts) the same way core/config.ts and other consumers in this diff do.
